justification: S2 increment 1 — the typed service->brief boundary, applied to the flood service (the worst key bug, #589: jrc_occurrence_pct vs jrc_water_occurrence_pct). Design choice: do NOT retype the services' return values (they emit dicts that the Trigger.dev relays depend on); instead define a Pydantic CONTRACT model (FloodServiceOutput) at the brief's consumption seam that is the single source of truth for the flood output key names. _build_flood_detail now parses the raw outputs through the contract and reads TYPED attributes (out.jrc_water_occurrence_pct) instead of loose .get('...'), so a typo or a service rename is a static/type error, not a silent null. Values stay nullable (genuine empty preserved); extra service keys (jrc_data_year, refused) are ignored. A contract test locks the model's fields to the documented service emit-keys so the brief's contract can't silently drift; the live drift check (S3) will re-capture real output against it. This is increment 1 of an incremental rollout (bushfire/shadow next).

pre_impl.existing_data: flood_truth.run_flood emits a dict with outputs.{epi_flood_class,epi_flood_label,jrc_water_occurrence_pct,dea_wofs_frequency_pct,bom_gauge_distance_km,flood_studies}; _build_flood_detail read them via loose .get. The Trigger.dev relay consumes the same dict.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A naive 'services return Pydantic models' would break the dict-consuming Trigger.dev relays; the contract must live at the brief seam, not in the service signature.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reused the existing FloodDetail schema; added a typed contract model + switched the build to typed reads. No service signature change.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A flood output that drops/renames a key now nulls the affected typed field (same visible-empty as before for that one field) but the contract test + S3 drift check surface the drift; extra keys are tolerated.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend only. 180 brief tests pass incl 5 new contract tests.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: the brief read flood keys by raw string; a service rename silently nulled a card (the #589 bug). After: the keys are a typed contract; a brief-side typo is a static error and a service rename is caught by the contract/drift test.

functions.name: _build_flood_detail
functions.input: the raw flood-service dict with an outputs sub-dict
functions.output: a FloodDetail built by reading typed attributes off the FloodServiceOutput contract rather than loose dict .get calls
functions.if_none: a falsy flood_raw returns None; an outputs dict missing a key yields that typed field as None

functions.name: FloodServiceOutput
functions.input: the flood service outputs dict via model_validate
functions.output: a typed object exposing the flood output keys as nullable attributes, ignoring extra service keys
functions.if_none: a missing key parses to None rather than raising, preserving a genuine empty

values: N/A - flood screening percentages, not regulatory values.

break_it.scenario: The flood service legitimately omits a key in a partial result
break_it.what_happens: that typed field is None, not a parse crash
break_it.how: contract fields are Optional with defaults, so a missing key is None (the card shows it unavailable), never an exception that drops the whole flood section. Guarded by test_flood_genuine_empty_values_preserved

break_it.scenario: The flood service adds a new output key
break_it.what_happens: parsing must tolerate the new key and not raise
break_it.repro: outputs with an unknown extra key
break_it.how: model_config extra=ignore tolerates new keys. Guarded by test_flood_contract_parses_real_shaped_output (jrc_data_year/refused extras)

break_it.scenario: Someone renames a flood key in the service back to the old name
break_it.what_happens: the correct contract field stays None (a regression), and the lock test fails if the brief contract is edited to match without updating the expected-keys set
break_it.how: the contract reads the correct key; test_flood_old_renamed_key_does_not_populate documents it and test_flood_contract_fields_are_the_expected_service_keys locks the field set; the S3 drift check (next) re-validates against real output

post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the Trigger.dev flood consumer still gets the same dict; only the brief's read changed.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run a brief — the flood card behaves identically (it reads the same keys, now typed). The contract test locks the flood output shape.
